deployment.commit_message:
GAP-FILL: real shrink-back-to-circle button for the expanded chat

Adam, describing his own intended interaction model directly: "I should be
able to move it over [to] not have it be front and center or I can shrink
it when it goes back to the circle that always stays."

Click-to-chat (prior commit) covered expand; there was no explicit way
back except manually dragging the window edge smaller. Added a real native
NSButton (SF Symbol, top drag strip, visible only while expanded) wired to
handleShrinkTapped() -- resizes straight back to badge size (120x120,
matching main.swift's initialSize) using the same window.setFrame() API
already proven live by expandToChat() and the continuously-running wander
timer. Repositioning without closing ("move it over") was already possible
via the same drag strip -- not a new gap, noted honestly rather than
rebuilt.

Real build.sh compile clean, relaunched the live process. Honestly not
click-tested: tried raw CGEvent injection (same dead end as the prior
click-to-chat commit) and System Events window-resize scripting (silently
no-op on this window type) -- both consistent with a structurally
hard-to-automate borderless/accessory NSWindow, not a code defect. Real
click verification from Adam still needed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
